_schema.description: Per-family benchmark spec for .github/workflows/speech-benchmark-desktop.yml. Kept out of YAML so it can be edited without touching the workflow, actionlint-diffed independently, and shared with local runs of scripts/benchmarks/run-family.sh.

fields.cmake_target: Ninja/CMake target(s) to build. Multiple targets space-separated.
fields.bench_kind: 'native' when the engine ships a *-bench binary or a --bench mode that we invoke once and parse the emitted JSON; 'time-wrapped' when we shell-time N invocations of a CLI and take the median wall-clock ourselves.
fields.binary: Path (relative to build/) of the executable to invoke.
fields.source: Where to fetch models from. 's3' (default) uses aws s3 cp against s3://$MODEL_S3_BUCKET/qvac_models_compiled/ggml/<s3_prefix>/<key>. 'huggingface' uses curl against https://huggingface.co/<hf_repo>/resolve/<hf_ref>/<name> — vanilla whisper GGMLs (ggml-tiny.bin etc.) live on HuggingFace, not S3.
fields.s3_prefix: Prefix under s3://$MODEL_S3_BUCKET/qvac_models_compiled/ggml/. All entries in `models` are downloaded to models/<family>/<basename> from this prefix — the intermediate directory segments (dates etc.) are dropped in the local layout.
fields.coreml_compare_on_darwin: Run the native benchmark twice on Darwin: required Core ML first, then the same command with PARAKEET_COREML_DISABLE=1 as the ggml baseline.
fields.models: List of files to fetch. Only the trailing filename lands in models/<family>/ — intermediate directory segments (dates etc.) are dropped locally. For source='s3' an entry is an S3 key string or a {s3, as} object (fetched as `as`). For source='huggingface' families other than whisper, an entry is a {name, sha256?} object resolved against hf_repo@hf_ref.
fields.hf_repo: HuggingFace repo id (e.g. 'ggerganov/whisper.cpp'). Required when source='huggingface'.
fields.hf_ref: HuggingFace ref (commit SHA) pinned so the download can't silently drift with upstream re-uploads. Required when source='huggingface'.
fields.models_by_size: Only for the whisper family. Object keyed by size ('tiny' / 'base' / 'small'). Each value is either a {name, sha256?} object (source='huggingface') or a list of S3 keys (source='s3'). sha256 is optional; when set the download is verified against it via sha256sum/shasum.
fields.args: Command-line arguments as a JSON array (one element per argv token, so multi-word values stay a single token). Placeholders expanded by run-family.sh per-element: ${MODEL_DIR}, ${MODELS_ROOT}, ${AUDIO_DIR}, ${MODEL_PATH}, and for bench_kind=native also ${RUNS}, ${WARMUP}, ${JSON_OUT}. Native families put the runs/warmup/json-out flags in `args` because their spellings differ (--json-out vs --bench-json, --runs vs --bench-runs).
fields.audio_duration_seconds: Length of the reference input audio (for ASR) or requested output audio (for TTS/music). Used to compute wall-based RTF when the bench binary does not report one. Null when the wall-clock isn't a fair RTF proxy (e.g. TTS with variable-length output).
fields.correctness: Optional. When present, run-family.sh computes an accuracy metric against a reference and merges it into result.json as wer_median (kind='wer'), der_median (kind='der'), or f1_median (kind='f1'). Object shape by kind: {kind:'wer', reference:'<repo-relative transcript path>', normalizer:'english'|'none'} for ASR; {kind:'der', reference:'<repo-relative RTTM path>', collar_ms:N} for diarization (collar_ms default 250); {kind:'f1', reference:'<repo-relative JSON-array path>', tolerance_ms:N} for VAD (frame-based precision/recall/F1, tolerance_ms default 100). Hypothesis source depends on bench_kind: native families supply it via `.transcript` in --json-out (parakeet WER); time-wrapped families supply it via the CLI's captured stdout (whisper -nt for WER; parakeet-cli --emit jsonl for sortformer DER; whisper-vad-speech-segments --no-prints for VAD F1). TTS uses {kind:tts_intelligibility, reference:prompt-file, asr_model:{repo,revision,name,sha256}}; TTS_TEXT and TTS_AUDIO_OUT placeholders supply the fixed prompt and generated WAV. TTS results are in tts_intelligibility, not wer_median. Absent block == correctness step skipped.
fields.notes: Free text; surfaced in the summary table's 'notes' column.

whisper.notes: Real ASR wall-time via whisper-cli on jfk.wav (11.0 s). RTF is wall_ms / 11000 — meaningful because the input is fixed-length. -nt suppresses timestamps in transcript output, which is what makes the time-wrapped correctness path viable: whisper-cli's stdout under -nt is just the decoded text, so run-family.sh feeds the captured stdout to compute-wer.py directly. Reference is the JFK-inaugural expected transcript shared with parakeet — same audio, same ref, so a whisper vs parakeet WER delta is a real model-quality delta, not a normalizer difference. Vanilla whisper GGMLs live on HuggingFace; hf_ref is the commit whisper-ci.yml pins.

parakeet.notes: TDT benchmark. On Darwin the driver requires the Core ML encoder for one run, repeats the same benchmark with PARAKEET_COREML_DISABLE=1, and reports encoder/end-to-end speedups. The TDT decoder remains on ggml Metal. jfk.wav is a ~11 s fixture; RTF < 1 means faster than real-time. Correctness: WER of the benchmark transcript against the checked-in reference; a non-trivial WER means either the model regressed or the reference drifted with a checkpoint bump.

sortformer.notes: Pure batch diarization: a Sortformer GGUF at --model takes parakeet-cli's diarize path (sortformer-4spk-v1 is the batch checkpoint; diar_streaming_sortformer_4spk-v2.1 belongs to the streaming API). The CLI's --bench mode covers transcription models only — the diarize and attributed paths return before the bench loop and emit no --bench-json — so the family is time-wrapped; wall includes model load like every time-wrapped row. Audio switched from jfk.wav (11 s, single speaker — trivial DER) to abcba.wav (~160.6 s, 3 speakers A-B-C-B-A) so DER actually stress-tests diarization; RTF divides by the abcba.wav duration. --emit jsonl makes parakeet-cli print one {speaker,start,end} JSON object per segment on stdout, which run-family.sh feeds to compute-der.py as the hypothesis. --n-gpu-layers 999 asks parakeet-cli to offload the encoder to a GPU when one is registered — parakeet-cli defaults to 0 (CPU-only) unlike whisper-cli which defaults to on, so the flag is needed for the macOS Metal path; on hosted Linux without a GPU-compiled ggml it falls back to CPU as a no-op. Correctness: DER against the checked-in abcba.rttm with a 250 ms collar; healthy sortformer scores single-digit percent.

vad.notes: Silero VAD v5.1.2 via the whisper-vad-speech-segments example on jfk.wav (11.0 s). --use-gpu takes the QVAC-24420-validated GPU path (Metal on the macOS runner) and falls back to CPU on GPU-less builds. --no-prints suppresses the example's non-result chatter so stdout carries only 'Detected N speech segments:' + 'Speech segment N: start=X, end=Y' lines — the compute-f1.py parser expects exactly that whisper.cpp example format and skips anything else with a stderr diagnostic (defensive against upstream format drift). UNITS GOTCHA: whisper.cpp's VAD API stores segment times in CENTISECONDS (see src/whisper.cpp samples_to_cs / _WHISPER_VAD_SEG_RE) and the example prints them raw without dividing, so 'Speech segment 0: start = 29.00' is 0.29 s, not 29 s. compute-f1.py's whisper-vad text parser divides by 100 to get seconds; the JSON-array shape uses seconds directly. Correctness: frame-based F1 against a hand-labeled reference for jfk.wav (one continuous 'Ask not…' segment, ~0.30-10.90 s) with a 100 ms boundary-tolerance collar — the standard VAD-eval collar convention.

chatterbox.notes: Fixed English TTS prompt; final measured WAV transcribed by pinned Whisper Tiny on CPU, then scored against the prompt. TTS WER is a single-output intelligibility proxy, including ASR errors, not a quality gate or median. ASR runs outside synthesis timing. This prompt resets the performance baseline.

audio8.notes: audio8-cli has no --bench flag; wall-clock via time. Runs on CPU (no --n-gpu-layers in args) and prints no backend marker of its own — the driver's GPU-evidence scrape / CPU default labels the Backend column. RTF omitted (text-driven variable output).

audio8-tts.notes: Fixed English TTS prompt; final measured WAV transcribed by pinned Whisper Tiny on CPU, then scored against the prompt. TTS WER is a single-output intelligibility proxy, including ASR errors, not a quality gate or median. ASR runs outside synthesis timing. This prompt resets the performance baseline. Separate full-TTS workload from the audio8 codec-quality benchmark in PR #244.

lavasr.notes: lavasr-bench emits stdout tables but has no --json-out; time-wrapped. No q8_0 in registry — f16 weights only.

acestep.notes: ~5 GB combined; hosted-linux runners may skip if the per-runner disk budget is exceeded. --dur 4 gives a deterministic RTF baseline.
